extracted.intended_audience: AAAI-25 paper authors and program committee reviewers (prospective submitters and reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and review-process guidance for submitting and reviewing full papers to the AAAI-25 Main Technical Track, including two-phase review mechanics, double-blind requirements, citation guidance, and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 1 reviewer allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Every paper will be allocated two reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a paper receives two reviews that are both sufficiently negative, it will be rejected without any opportunity for author feedback. Phase 1 uses the abstract deadline (Aug 7, 2024) and full paper deadline (Aug 15, 2024) as submission milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 1 early-rejection rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers receiving two sufficiently negative Phase 1 reviews are rejected without author feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an automatic/summary-style cutoff between Phase 1 and Phase 2; authors of such papers will not receive a feedback window to respond. The threshold is described as 'sufficiently negative' and exercised at the discretion of the reviewing chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 2 reviewer allocation and independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Remaining (non-Phase-1-rejected) papers progress to Phase 2 and will be allocated additional reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase 2 reviewers will not be given access to Phase 1 reviews until after submitting their own reviews — preserving independent assessment. After Phase 2 reviews are collected, the program committee and senior program committee will engage in discussion taking author feedback into account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author feedback window
rubrics_metrics.description: A single author feedback phase allows authors of Phase 2 papers to comment on all reviews (from both phases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author feedback window runs from November 4–8. Author comments will be taken into account in the subsequent program committee discussion and in final decision-making. Only papers that progress past Phase 1 receive this feedback opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind review requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: AAAI-25 reviews are double blind: neither reviewers nor authors should be able to identify each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first page (where the paper body begins) may include the title, abstract, content areas, and ID number (if available), but must not include author names or affiliations. Acknowledgments of funding or assistance should also be omitted. Ensure no information is included that would identify the authors or their affiliations; papers including such information may be summarily rejected at the discretion of the program chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omission of identifying information (acknowledgments/funding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledgments of funding or assistance should be omitted from submissions to preserve anonymity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly remove funding statements, institutional identifiers in acknowledgments, and other signals of identity from the submitted version; inclusion can lead to summary rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing previous published literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions should include references to all published literature relevant to the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure complete citations to relevant published work; this helps reviewers place the contribution and assess novelty/relatedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for citing authors' own previous work
rubrics_metrics.description: When the authors’ previous work is relevant, authors have three options (in descending order of desirability): use third-person phrasing; avoid citing previous unpublished work that would identify the authors; or cite suppressed work as 'Anonymous (2019)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred: use the third person (e.g., 'Previously, Hinton et al (2006) showed that…' rather than 'In our previous work...'). Avoid citing previous unpublished work (e.g., technical reports or PhD theses that would identify authors); such citations may be added to the camera-ready copy. If neither option is appropriate, cite as 'Anonymous (2019)' to indicate a suppressed citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint and research-talk exception to anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: Two cases where existence of non-anonymous online material will not be considered a violation: (1) submitted work appears as an unrefereed preprint (e.g., on arXiv) or in a workshop without archival proceedings; (2) the work has been discussed in research talks with abstracts/videos online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even in these cases, the AAAI-25 submission should not include citations or other pointers to the non-anonymous material, and the non-anonymous online material should not reference the fact that the work was submitted to AAAI-25; violations may lead to summary rejection. Reviewers will be instructed not to actively seek out such previous publications or to share knowledge of them with other reviewers, but they will not be disqualified if they encounter such information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty for violating blind-review policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers including identifying information or otherwise violating the blind-review policy may be summarily rejected at the discretion of the program chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program chairs may exercise summary rejection for violations; authors should proactively remove identifying cues. Reviewers who happen upon identifying material are not automatically disqualified, but the policy discourages actively seeking such material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer behavior regarding Phase 1 reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase 2 reviewers will not have access to Phase 1 reviews until after they submit their own reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule is intended to prevent bias from earlier assessments and to promote independent evaluation in Phase 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission deadlines and material deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Key deadlines (all 'anywhere on earth' UTC-12) include: web site open July 8, 2024; abstracts due Aug 7, 2024; full papers due Aug 15, 2024; supplementary material and code due Aug 19, 2024; Phase 1 notifications Oct 14, 2024; author feedback Nov 4–8, 2024; final decisions Dec 9, 2024; camera-ready due Dec 19, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines are track-specific and may differ; authors must check track CFPs for exact dates. Supplementary material (including code) has its own deadline. All times are 'anywhere on earth' (UTC-12). Missing or late submissions may affect consideration.
